en.title: The Book of Dao · Chapter Five · Keeping the Middle
en.原文:
天地不仁
以萬物為芻狗
聲人不仁
以百省為芻狗

天地之閒
其猶橐籥輿
虛而不淈
蹱而俞出

多聞數竆
不若守於中
en.字龕:
### 芻 *chú* 狗 — the straw dog

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![芻之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E8%8A%BB.svg) ![狗之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E7%8B%97.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「芻，刈艸也。象包束艸之形。」 — "Mown grass. The graph pictures a bundle of grass bound up."

**像 Image** ｜ A bundle of grass tied into the shape of a dog. For the rite it is set on the altar and honored; the rite done, it is thrown to the roadside. The graph itself is that bundle — honored and discarded, and the grass indifferent to both.

**義 Sense** ｜ Heaven and earth's "inhumanity" is not cruelty: it is impartiality. Things are honored in their season and let go in their season — no favoritism in the keeping, no resentment in the dropping. The sage's is the same.

### 橐 *tuó* 籥 *yuè* — the bellows （複合龕 · compound niche）

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![橐之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E6%A9%90.svg) ![籥之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E7%B1%A5.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「橐，囊也。」 — "A bag." 「籥，書僮竹笘也。」 — "a bamboo slip-tube for a writing pupil" (here, borrowed for the bellows-pipe).

**像 Image** ｜ A skin bag with a bamboo pipe: the smith's bellows. Press it, and wind comes out; let go, and it fills again — the bag works *because* it is empty. The busier it is, the more wind.

**義 Sense** ｜ Heaven-and-earth between is one great bellows: empty and never drained, moving and ever more issuing. Fullness would be its death; emptiness is its inexhaustible use.

### 中 *zhōng* — the middle

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![中之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E4%B8%AD.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「中，內也。從口。丨，上下通。」 — "The inside. From 口, the enclosure; 丨 piercing through above and below." In bronze script the graph is a banner-pole planted at the center, its streamers flying.

**像 Image** ｜ A banner-pole set at the center of the host — the thing everyone rallies by, pierced straight through, top to bottom. The middle is not the halfway point on a scale; it is the pole everything else gathers around.

**義 Sense** ｜ "Keep to the middle" is not splitting the difference between saying much and saying little. It is holding the empty pole-center where hearing and reckoning have not yet begun to spin.

en.校記:
The chapter follows Manuscript A (MS A) throughout, except that 天地之閒, damaged in MS A, follows Manuscript B (MS B), and 以百省為芻狗 combines the two. Graphs are those outside the brackets in the *Changsha Mawangdui Han mu jianbo jicheng* (2014; hereafter *Jicheng*).

- 聲人不仁: Follows MS A. MS A writes 聲人, MS B 𦔻人 (耳 beside 口); both are read as 聖人 "the sage".
- 以百省為芻狗: The manuscripts complement each other. MS A reads 以百省□□狗, with 為芻 lost; in MS B 以 is lost and the text has 百姓. The *Jicheng* reads MS A's 省 as 姓 "clan". Wang Bi has 以百姓為芻狗.
- 天地之閒: Follows MS B. In MS A 之 is lost; its 閒, given as a lacuna in Gao Ming's transcription, is read directly by the *Jicheng*. Both manuscripts write 閒, read as 間 "between".
- 其猶橐籥輿: Follows MS A, whose 其 is read directly by the *Jicheng*. MS B reads 亓猷橐籥輿; Gao Ming's transcription gives 其猶橐籥與, but the plate shows 猷 and 輿. 猷 is read as 猶 "like", 輿 as the question particle 歟. Wang Bi has 其猶橐籥乎.
- 虛而不淈: The manuscripts agree; 淈 is read as 屈 "to be exhausted". Wang Bi has 虛而不屈.
- 蹱而俞出: Follows MS A, which writes 蹱 (足 with 童), read by the *Jicheng* as 動 "to move". A collation slip suggested that the *Jicheng* prints 踵 (足 with 重), but the print, enlarged, shows 蹱, as does Gao Ming's transcription. MS B writes 勭, also read as 動. 俞 is read as 愈 "the more". Wang Bi has 動而愈出.
- 多聞數竆: Follows MS A. MS A writes 竆 and MS B a variant of 窮 (身 and 巳 under 穴); the *Jicheng* reads both as 窮 "to run out". Both manuscripts have 多聞 "much hearing"; Wang Bi has 多言 "much speaking".
- 不若守於中: The manuscripts agree; Wang Bi has 不如守中.
en.疏:
杳眇曰：

夫道一章之要在虛用，而虛用之要在守中，此三義環環相扣者也。

天地不仁，以萬物為芻狗。天地無心，而任物自化。芻狗者，祭祀之草偶，用時奉之，用畢棄之，天地以待萬物，無偏愛之私，亦無厭棄之怨，此道之公也。《論語》有云：「君子之於天下也，無適也，無莫也。」聖人不仁，正斯義爾——非無仁心之偏，乃成其大公之仁爾。

橐籥之喻，正明虛用之妙。帛書作「虛而不淈」，王弼本作「屈」——淈者水竭之義，屈者受限之謂，二字淺深自見。帛書之意：虛空無有竭盡之時，愈鼓而風愈出，此虛之容量無限故也。道經「道用」章言「道沖而用之有弗盈」，其旨一也。天曰虛、地曰靜，虛者橐籥之本，有生於無，此生化之樞機也。

守中者，守虛也。帛書作「多聞數竆」，王弼本作「多言」——聞者博學而炫於外，言者馳說而窮於辯，二者皆屬有為，擾心之虛而速其竭也。《大學》言「知止而後有定」，《中庸》言「喜怒哀樂之未發謂之中」，皆守中守虛之旨，儒道相通，固如是爾。

是故守中者，守虛也；虛者，芻狗之象也；橐籥者，虛用之器也。三義一貫，聖人无為之旨備矣。學者茍能會此，則知不仁之為仁大矣。
en.疏英:
Yaomiao says:

The crux of this chapter is empty use, and the crux of empty use is keeping the middle — three rings of one chain.

"Heaven and earth are not humane: they treat the ten thousand things as straw dogs." Heaven and earth have no heart, and let things transform of themselves. The straw dog is a grass effigy for the rite — set up and honored while the rite lasts, thrown aside when it ends. So heaven and earth treat the ten thousand things: no private fondness in the keeping, no grudge in the dropping — the impartiality of the Dao. The Analects: "the noble man, toward all-under-heaven, has nothing he is for and nothing he is against." The sage's "inhumanity" is the same sense — not the absence of a humane heart, but the great impartial humaneness made complete.

The bellows image makes the subtlety of empty use plain. The silk text writes 虛而不淈, "empty and never drained," where Wang Bi has 不屈, "unyielding." 淈 is water running dry; 屈 is being bent within limits — the depths of the two graphs show themselves. The silk text's sense: the empty never runs out — the more you work it, the more wind issues — for the capacity of emptiness is limitless. The chapter "The Dao in Use" has it: "the Dao is hollow, yet in use it never fills" — one point. Heaven is called empty, earth is called still: emptiness is the root of the bellows, presence is born of absence — the pivot of all generating.

"Keep to the middle" is keeping to the empty. The silk text has 多聞數竆, "much hearing soon runs out," where Wang Bi has 多言, "much talk." 聞 is broad learning flaunted outward; 言 is racing speech that argues itself dry — both belong to contrivance, stirring the heart's emptiness so it drains the faster. The Great Learning says "know where to stop, and only then is there steadiness"; the Doctrine of the Mean, "before joy, anger, grief, and delight are stirred — that is called the middle." Both are the keeping of the middle and the empty — Confucian and Daoist running together, as they so often do.

So: keeping the middle is keeping the empty; the empty is the straw-dog image; the bellows is the instrument of empty use. Three senses, one thread — the sage's non-doing complete. Let the student gather this, and he will know: the inhumanity is the greatest humaneness of all.
en.英譯:
Heaven and earth are not humane (不仁): they treat the ten thousand things as straw dogs (芻狗). The sage is not humane: he treats the hundred clans as straw dogs.

The space between heaven and earth — is it not like a bellows (橐籥)? Empty, and never drained (不淈); move it, and ever more comes out.

Much hearing soon runs out. Better to keep to the middle (守於中).

帛書甲乙.乙: 天地不仁以萬物為芻狗𦔻人不仁□百姓為芻狗天地之閒亓猷橐籥輿虛而不淈勭而俞出多聞數窮不若守於中
帛書甲乙.甲: 天地不仁以萬物為芻狗∠聲人不仁∠以百省□□狗天地□閒其猶橐籥輿虛而不淈蹱而俞出多聞數竆不若守於中

校記:
本章除「天地之閒」一句甲本殘泐據乙本，「以百省為芻狗」甲乙互足外，皆據甲本；字從《集成》（2014）括號外原字。

- 聲人不仁：從甲本。甲作「聲人」，乙作⿰耳口之「𦔻人」，皆讀為「聖人」。
- 以百省為芻狗：甲乙互足。甲本作「以百省□□狗」，「為芻」二字殘；乙本「以」字殘，作「百姓」。甲「省」，《集成》讀為「姓」。王弼本作「以百姓為芻狗」。
- 天地之閒：據乙本。甲本「之」字殘，「閒」字《集成》直接釋出，高明實錄作缺。甲乙皆作「閒」，讀為「間」。
- 其猶橐籥輿：從甲本，「其」字《集成》直接釋出。乙本作「亓猷橐籥輿」，高明實錄作「其猶橐籥與」，圖版作「猷」「輿」；「猷」讀為「猶」，「輿」讀為「歟」。王弼本作「其猶橐籥乎」。
- 虛而不淈：甲乙同，「淈」讀為「屈」；王弼本作「虛而不屈」。
- 蹱而俞出：從甲本。甲作足旁童之「蹱」，《集成》讀為「動」；勘誤或謂印本作足旁重之「踵」，放大審之實作「蹱」，高明實錄亦同。乙本作「勭」，亦讀為「動」。「俞」讀為「愈」。王弼本作「動而愈出」。
- 多聞數竆：從甲本。甲作「竆」，乙作窮之異寫（穴下身巳），《集成》皆讀為「窮」。甲乙皆作「多聞」，王弼本作「多言」。
- 不若守於中：甲乙同；王弼本作「不如守中」。
